name: Exchange from spin algebra and Pauli exclusion
summary: Heisenberg exchange arises because the Coulomb energy depends on the singlet or triplet spin state through antisymmetry; addition of spin angular momenta gives the S1.S2 form.

name: Spin angular momentum as a transport degree of freedom
summary: Spintronics transports and manipulates spin angular momentum: spin precession, spin-orbit coupling (Rashba/Dresselhaus) and spin-transfer torque are the quantum mechanics of spin applied to devices.
map: \dot{\mathbf S}=\gamma\mathbf S\times\mathbf B;\ H_R=\alpha(\boldsymbol\sigma\times\mathbf k)\cdot\hat z
sources: Žutić, Fabian & Das Sarma (2004). "Spintronics: Fundamentals and applications". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 76, 323. [arXiv:cond-mat/0405528](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0405528)

name: Kitaev honeycomb model and Kitaev materials
summary: Kitaev's exactly solvable honeycomb model has a Z2 spin-liquid ground state with Majorana excitations; it motivates the search in alpha-RuCl3 and iridates.
sources: Kitaev (2006). "Anyons in an exactly solved model and beyond". *Ann. Phys.* 321, 2. [arXiv:cond-mat/0506438](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0506438)

name: Landau levels are harmonic-oscillator levels
summary: A charged particle in a uniform field maps onto a harmonic oscillator, giving Landau levels; filling them gives the integer quantum Hall plateaus.

name: Aharonov-Bohm oscillations in mesoscopic rings
summary: Phase-coherent electrons in metal rings show conductance oscillations with flux period h/e, a direct transport measurement of the Aharonov-Bohm phase.
sources: Webb et al. (1985). "Observation of h/e Aharonov-Bohm Oscillations in Normal-Metal Rings". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 54, 2696. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.54.2696](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.54.2696)

name: Berry phase pi of graphene's Dirac electrons
summary: Pseudospin winding gives graphene electrons a pi Berry phase, producing the half-integer quantum Hall sequence and suppressed backscattering.
sources: Zhang, Tan, Stormer & Kim (2005). "Experimental observation of the quantum Hall effect and Berry's phase in graphene". *Nature* 438, 201. [arXiv:cond-mat/0509355](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0509355)

name: Emergent electromagnetism of skyrmions
summary: Electrons adiabatically following a skyrmion texture acquire a real-space Berry phase that acts as an emergent magnetic flux of one quantum per skyrmion, giving the topological Hall effect.
sources: Nagaosa & Tokura (2013). "Topological properties and dynamics of magnetic skyrmions". *Nature Nanotechnol.* 8, 899. [doi:10.1038/nnano.2013.243](https://doi.org/10.1038/nnano.2013.243)

name: Anyon statistics as Berry phases
summary: Exchanging two quasiparticles adiabatically gives a Berry phase; for Laughlin quasiholes it equals pi times the filling, so fractional statistics is a geometric phase.
sources: Arovas, Schrieffer & Wilczek (1984). "Fractional Statistics and the Quantum Hall Effect". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 53, 722. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.53.722](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.53.722)

name: Geometric phases organize topological matter
summary: Berry's 1984 phase gave condensed matter a unified language for polarization, anomalous Hall effects and topological phases.
sources: Xiao, Chang & Niu (2010). "Berry phase effects on electronic properties". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 1959. [arXiv:0907.2021](https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.2021)

name: Chern number is integrated Berry curvature
summary: The Hall conductance of a filled band equals the Brillouin-zone integral of Berry curvature (TKNN); geometric-phase concepts define all band-topological invariants.
sources: Berry (1984). "Quantal phase factors accompanying adiabatic changes". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 392, 45. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1984.0023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1984.0023)

Thouless, Kohmoto, Nightingale & den Nijs (1982). "Quantized Hall Conductance in a Two-Dimensional Periodic Potential". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 49, 405. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.405](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.405)
Xiao, Chang & Niu (2010). "Berry phase effects on electronic properties". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 1959. [arXiv:0907.2021](https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.2021)

name: Weyl points as Berry-curvature monopoles
summary: Berry's degeneracy monopole is realized in crystals: Weyl nodes are sources of Berry flux with integer charge, giving Fermi arcs and the chiral anomaly.
sources: Berry (1984). "Quantal phase factors accompanying adiabatic changes". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 392, 45. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1984.0023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1984.0023)

Wan et al. (2011). "Topological semimetal and Fermi-arc surface states in the electronic structure of pyrochlore iridates". *Phys. Rev. B* 83, 205101. [arXiv:1007.0016](https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.0016)

name: Path-integral quantum Monte Carlo
summary: Imaginary-time path integrals map quantum many-body systems onto classical polymers, sampled by Monte Carlo; bosonic exchange appears as permutation cycles (superfluid helium).
sources: Ceperley (1995). "Path integrals in the theory of condensed helium". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 67, 279. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.67.279](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.67.279)

name: Born approximation behind diffraction
summary: X-ray, electron and neutron diffraction are first-Born scattering: the cross section is the Fourier transform of the scattering density, and inelastic neutron scattering measures the dynamic structure factor.
sources: Van Hove (1954). "Correlations in Space and Time and Born Approximation Scattering in Systems of Interacting Particles". *Phys. Rev.* 95, 249. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.95.249](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.95.249)

name: Kondo effect as resonant scattering
summary: Below T_K conduction electrons scatter off the Kondo singlet with phase shift pi/2, the unitary limit; the Friedel sum rule ties the phase shift to the screened charge.

name: Cavity QED with quantum dots
summary: Single quantum dots in photonic-crystal nanocavities reach strong coupling with vacuum Rabi splitting, the solid-state realization of Jaynes-Cummings physics.
sources: Yoshie et al. (2004). "Vacuum Rabi splitting with a single quantum dot in a photonic crystal nanocavity". *Nature* 432, 200. [doi:10.1038/nature03119](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature03119)

name: Strong coupling of excitons to cavity photons
summary: Excitons in microcavities reach strong coupling, forming polaritons with vacuum Rabi splitting, the Jaynes-Cummings physics of cavity QED with a collective emitter.
sources: Kasprzak et al. (2006). "Bose–Einstein condensation of exciton polaritons". *Nature* 443, 409. [doi:10.1038/nature05131](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature05131)

name: Mechanical resonators are engineered phonons
summary: Optomechanical resonators are phonon modes of nanostructures; phononic band gaps, Brillouin scattering and two-level-system damping are lattice-dynamics physics.
sources: Aspelmeyer, Kippenberg & Marquardt (2014). "Cavity optomechanics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 86, 1391. [arXiv:1303.0733](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.0733)

name: Electron quantum optics
summary: Single-electron sources, quantum point contacts as beam splitters and edge channels as waveguides let electronic HOM and HBT experiments mirror photon statistics; shot noise is the fermionic g2.
sources: Bocquillon et al. (2013). "Coherence and Indistinguishability of Single Electrons Emitted by Independent Sources". *Science* 339, 1054. [doi:10.1126/science.1232572](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1232572)

name: Quantum-dot single-photon sources
summary: Self-assembled semiconductor quantum dots are two-level emitters that, embedded in micropillars, give bright, pure and indistinguishable single photons.
sources: Michler et al. (2000). "A Quantum Dot Single-Photon Turnstile Device". *Science* 290, 2282. [doi:10.1126/science.290.5500.2282](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.290.5500.2282)

name: Quantum emitters in 2D semiconductors
summary: Strain- and defect-localized excitons in monolayer WSe2 act as single-photon emitters, linking 2D-material excitonics to quantum-optical sources.
sources: Srivastava et al. (2015). "Optically active quantum dots in monolayer WSe2". *Nature Nanotechnol.* 10, 491. [doi:10.1038/nnano.2015.60](https://doi.org/10.1038/nnano.2015.60)

name: Superconducting single-photon detectors
summary: SNSPDs and transition-edge sensors use photon-induced breaking of superconductivity (hotspots, steep R(T)) to count photons with high efficiency and low jitter.
sources: Gol'tsman et al. (2001). "Picosecond superconducting single-photon optical detector". *Appl. Phys. Lett.* 79, 705. [doi:10.1063/1.1388868](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1388868)

name: Area laws: black-hole and entanglement entropy
summary: Entanglement entropy of a field across a surface scales with its area, as does Bekenstein-Hawking entropy; in gapped topological phases the area law has a universal constant correction -gamma = -ln D, the same diagnostic used for long-range entanglement.
breaks: The entanglement coefficient alpha is cutoff-dependent; matching 1/4G needs renormalization of Newton's constant, while gamma has no BH counterpart.
sources: Srednicki (1993). "Entropy and area". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 71, 666. [arXiv:hep-th/9303048](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9303048)
Kitaev & Preskill (2006). "Topological Entanglement Entropy". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 96, 110404. [arXiv:hep-th/0510092](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0510092)

name: SYK: strange metal and near-extremal black hole
summary: The Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model of randomly interacting fermions, rooted in a random-magnet spin fluid, has an extensive zero-temperature entropy and emergent reparametrization symmetry matching near-extremal charged black holes and JT gravity in AdS2; it also maximizes chaos.
sources: Sachdev (2015). "Bekenstein-Hawking Entropy and Strange Metals". *Phys. Rev. X* 5, 041025. [arXiv:1506.05111](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.05111)
Maldacena & Stanford (2016). "Remarks on the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model". *Phys. Rev. D* 94, 106002. [arXiv:1604.07818](https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.07818)

name: Type-II Weyl cones as analogue horizons
summary: A tilted Weyl cone is a Weyl fermion in an effective Painleve-Gullstrand metric whose shift vector is the tilt; where the tilt exceeds the Fermi velocity (type I to type II) the cone tips over like light cones at a horizon, and Hawking-like tunnelling has been proposed at such interfaces.
map: H=\hbar\mathbf t\cdot\mathbf k+\hbar v_F\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf k\ \leftrightarrow\ ds^2=-c^2dt^2+(d\mathbf x-\mathbf v\,dt)^2,\ |\mathbf t|=v_F\ \text{at horizon}
breaks: No Einstein dynamics or backreaction; lattice cutoff, disorder and electron interactions are not small, and the emitted 'temperature' would be tiny.
sources: Volovik (2016). "Black hole and Hawking radiation by type-II Weyl fermions". *JETP Lett.* 104, 645. [arXiv:1610.00521](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.00521)

name: Chaos bound and Planckian dissipation
summary: Black holes saturate the bound on the Lyapunov exponent of out-of-time-order correlators and are the fastest scramblers; strange metals show a transport rate near the same Planckian scale k_B T/hbar, suggesting a common bound on dissipation in matter without quasiparticles.
breaks: No theorem ties lambda_L to the momentum-relaxation rate that sets resistivity; the chaos bound is rigorous, the transport 'bound' is empirical and has counterexamples.
sources: Maldacena, Shenker & Stanford (2016). "A bound on chaos". *JHEP* 08, 106. [arXiv:1503.01409](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.01409)
Sekino & Susskind (2008). "Fast Scramblers". *JHEP* 10, 065. [arXiv:0808.2096](https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.2096)

name: Dislocations as torsion, disclinations as curvature
summary: The continuum theory of crystal defects is Riemann-Cartan geometry: the Burgers vector is the closure failure (torsion) and the Frank angle the rotation holonomy (curvature); a disclination line has the conical metric of a cosmic string.
map: b^a=\oint e^a{}_\mu dx^\mu=\iint T^a\ (\text{torsion}),\quad \Omega=\iint R\ (\text{curvature});\ ds^2=dr^2+\alpha^2r^2d\phi^2+dz^2
breaks: Euclidean signature and elastic energy replace the Einstein-Hilbert action; the 'geometry' is a bookkeeping device with no propagating gravitons.

name: Hall viscosity and gravitational response
summary: Coupling a quantum Hall fluid to a background spatial metric and spin connection defines Hall viscosity eta_H = hbar s-bar n/2 and the Wen-Zee shift on curved surfaces; Luttinger's fictitious gravitational potential likewise defines thermal-Hall response.
map: \eta_H=\tfrac12\hbar\bar s\,n,\quad N_\phi=\nu^{-1}N-\mathcal S\ (\text{sphere}),\quad \mathcal L_{\rm WZ}\propto\frac{\nu\bar s}{2\pi}\omega\wedge dA
breaks: The background metric is a probe, not dynamical gravity, and the fluid is non-relativistic.
sources: Hoyos & Son (2012). "Hall Viscosity and Electromagnetic Response". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 108, 066805. [arXiv:1109.2651](https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.2651)
Luttinger (1964). "Theory of Thermal Transport Coefficients". *Phys. Rev.* 135, A1505. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.135.A1505](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.135.A1505)

name: Gravity Probe B gyroscopes read by SQUIDs
summary: Gravity Probe B measured geodetic and frame-dragging precession of niobium-coated quartz rotors through the London moment of the spinning superconductor, read out by SQUID magnetometers at milliarcsecond resolution.
sources: Everitt et al. (2011). "Gravity Probe B: Final Results of a Space Experiment to Test General Relativity". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 106, 221101. [arXiv:1105.3456](https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.3456)

name: Chiral 'graviton' modes of FQH liquids
summary: Haldane's geometric picture gives a fractional quantum Hall fluid a dynamical unimodular intrinsic metric; its long-wavelength fluctuation is a spin-2 chiral mode (GMP magnetoroton), whose chirality has been probed with circularly polarized Raman scattering, like a GW helicity-2 mode.
breaks: The mode is gapped, non-relativistic and lives on a lattice-free 2D fluid without diffeomorphism invariance; it is spin-2 only in the sense of its rotation quantum number.
sources: Haldane (2011). "Geometrical Description of the Fractional Quantum Hall Effect". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 107, 116801. [arXiv:1106.3375](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.3375)

name: Amorphous mirror coatings limit LIGO thermal noise
summary: In the most sensitive LIGO band the floor is Brownian thermal noise of the amorphous Ta2O5/SiO2 mirror coatings, set via fluctuation-dissipation by their mechanical loss angle, which comes from two-level systems in the glass.
map: S_x(f)=\frac{2k_BT}{\pi^2f^2}\frac{W_{\rm diss}}{F_0^2},\quad W_{\rm diss}\propto\phi_{\rm coat}\ (\text{loss angle})
sources: Levin (1998). "Internal thermal noise in the LIGO test masses: A direct approach". *Phys. Rev. D* 57, 659. [arXiv:gr-qc/9707013](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9707013)

name: Liquid crystals test cosmic-string network scaling
summary: Cosmic-string GW backgrounds rest on the Kibble mechanism and scaling of string networks; quenched nematic liquid crystals form and coarsen string networks that can be filmed, giving laboratory checks of defect formation and scaling.
breaks: Nematic strings move dissipatively, not relativistically (no Nambu-Goto dynamics), and do not radiate gravitational waves; loop production and GW spectra cannot be tested this way.
sources: Chuang, Durrer, Turok & Yurke (1991). "Cosmology in the Laboratory: Defect Dynamics in Liquid Crystals". *Science* 251, 1336. [doi:10.1126/science.251.4999.1336](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.251.4999.1336)

name: Cryogenic crystalline test masses
summary: KAGRA uses 20 K sapphire and Einstein Telescope/LIGO Voyager plan cryogenic silicon test masses, chosen for low phonon loss and for silicon's vanishing thermal expansion near 123 K, which kills thermoelastic noise.
sources: Punturo et al. (2010). "The Einstein Telescope: A third-generation gravitational wave observatory". *Class. Quantum Grav.* 27, 194002. [doi:10.1088/0264-9381/27/19/194002](https://doi.org/10.1088/0264-9381/27/19/194002)

name: Dirac-fluid hydrodynamics near the KSS bound
summary: Near charge neutrality graphene electrons form a nearly relativistic Dirac fluid with small eta/s and violated Wiedemann-Franz law; relativistic and holographic hydrodynamics developed for the QGP and black branes describe its transport.
breaks: Graphene is weakly coupled (alpha_g of order 1 but with log running), has disorder and phonons, and has no gravity dual.
sources: Crossno et al. (2016). "Observation of the Dirac fluid and the breakdown of the Wiedemann-Franz law in graphene". *Science* 351, 1058. [arXiv:1509.04713](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.04713)

name: MERA tensor networks as discrete AdS
summary: The multiscale entanglement renormalization ansatz built for critical spin chains has a hyperbolic network geometry; minimal cuts through it reproduce Ryu-Takayanagi, so condensed-matter numerics became a toy model of emergent bulk space and holographic codes.
sources: Swingle (2012). "Entanglement Renormalization and Holography". *Phys. Rev. D* 86, 065007. [arXiv:0905.1317](https://arxiv.org/abs/0905.1317)

name: Holographic strange metals (AdS/CMT)
summary: Charged black branes model compressible quantum-critical matter without quasiparticles: horizon geometry sets T-linear resistivity, Planckian relaxation and non-Fermi-liquid spectral functions in bottom-up holographic models.
breaks: No known microscopic lattice Hamiltonian has a controlled gravity dual; large-N and strong coupling are assumptions, and bottom-up models fit rather than derive cuprate data.
sources: Hartnoll (2009). "Lectures on holographic methods for condensed matter physics". *Class. Quantum Grav.* 26, 224002. [arXiv:0903.3246](https://arxiv.org/abs/0903.3246)

name: Holographic superconductors: hairy black holes
summary: Below a critical temperature a charged black brane becomes unstable to growing charged scalar hair; the boundary dual is a condensate that breaks U(1), with an optical-conductivity gap and a gap-to-Tc ratio larger than BCS.
breaks: The boundary U(1) is global, not dynamical, so there is no Meissner effect without extra gauging; mean-field exponents follow from large N.
sources: Hartnoll, Herzog & Horowitz (2008). "Building a Holographic Superconductor". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 101, 031601. [arXiv:0803.3295](https://arxiv.org/abs/0803.3295)

name: Emergent gauge fields and gravity from many-body order
summary: String-net condensation in lattice spin models gives emergent photons and fermions, raising the question of whether gravity can emerge the same way; emergent-gravity programmes (Volovik, Wen) use topological order as a template.
breaks: Weinberg-Witten forbids a massless spin-2 particle from a Lorentz-covariant conserved stress tensor, and emergent Lorentz invariance is not exact on a lattice; no model yields Einstein gravity.
sources: Levin & Wen (2005). "String-net condensation: A physical mechanism for topological phases". *Phys. Rev. B* 71, 045110. [arXiv:cond-mat/0404617](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0404617)
Weinberg & Witten (1980). "Limits on massless particles". *Phys. Lett. B* 96, 59. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(80)90212-9](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(80)90212-9)

name: Strained graphene: Dirac fields in curved space
summary: Low-energy graphene electrons obey a 2+1D Dirac equation; strain and ripples enter as pseudo-gauge fields and a position-dependent tetrad, so curved-space Dirac methods describe pseudo-Landau levels in nanobubbles and suggest Hawking/Unruh analogues.
breaks: v_F is 1e6 m/s, not c; Coulomb interactions are instantaneous, valleys carry opposite pseudo-fields, and the 'metric' is not dynamical.
sources: Vozmediano, Katsnelson & Guinea (2010). "Gauge fields in graphene". *Phys. Rep.* 496, 109. [arXiv:1003.5179](https://arxiv.org/abs/1003.5179)

name: Mixed axial-gravitational anomaly in Weyl semimetals
summary: The chiral anomaly of Weyl fermions has a gravitational piece proportional to the curvature, which via Luttinger's temperature-as-gravitational-potential maps to a thermal-gradient term; positive magneto-thermoelectric conductance in NbP was reported as its signature.
breaks: Thermal-transport signals have competing phonon and conventional explanations; the anomaly attribution is contested.
sources: Gooth et al. (2017). "Experimental signatures of the mixed axial-gravitational anomaly in the Weyl semimetal NbP". *Nature* 547, 324. [arXiv:1703.10682](https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.10682)

name: Emergent Lorentz boosts with c -> v_F in graphene
summary: Graphene's massless Dirac Hamiltonian is invariant under boosts with v_F replacing c; boosting away an in-plane E field predicts the collapse of Landau levels when E/B reaches v_F, as in E x B drift with E > cB.
breaks: Emergent symmetry only at low energy: trigonal warping, lattice and instantaneous Coulomb interaction break it.
sources: Lukose, Shankar & Baskaran (2007). "Novel Electric Field Effects on Landau Levels in Graphene". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 98, 116802. [arXiv:cond-mat/0611406](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0611406)

name: Spin-orbit coupling and Thomas precession
summary: An electron moving through an electric field sees a magnetic field B' = -v x E/c^2 in its rest frame; with the Thomas precession factor 1/2 this gives the spin-orbit coupling behind Rashba, Dresselhaus and spin Hall effects used in spintronics.
sources: Thomas (1926). "The Motion of the Spinning Electron". *Nature* 117, 514. [doi:10.1038/117514a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/117514a0)

name: Quantum-limited amplifiers for axion haloscopes
summary: Cavity haloscopes convert axions to microwave photons in a magnet; SQUID and Josephson parametric amplifiers (and squeezing) bring readout to the quantum limit, setting the scan rate in the micro-eV mass range.
sources: Sikivie (1983). "Experimental Tests of the Invisible Axion". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 51, 1415. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.51.1415](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.51.1415)

name: Axion electrodynamics in topological magnets
summary: The theta angle of a TI plays the role of the axion field; in magnetic TIs theta can fluctuate, giving a dynamical 'axion quasiparticle' whose coupling to E.B mirrors the QCD axion's photon coupling and has been proposed for dark-matter detection.
map: \mathcal L=\frac{\alpha}{4\pi^2}\theta(\mathbf x,t)\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B\ \leftrightarrow\ -\frac{g_{a\gamma\gamma}}{4}aF\tilde F,\ \theta\leftrightarrow a/f_a
breaks: The condensed-matter theta is an emergent, lattice-scale field with meV dynamics and no shift symmetry from a QCD anomaly; it cannot solve strong CP or be dark matter itself.
sources: Qi & Zhang (2011). "Topological insulators and superconductors". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 83, 1057. [arXiv:1008.2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.2026)

name: Sub-MeV dark matter scattering into phonons
summary: Below ~MeV, dark-matter momentum transfers match crystal phonon and magnon scales, so detection relies on condensed-matter response functions (dynamic structure factor, dielectric loss) rather than nuclear recoils.
sources: Zurek (2024). "Dark Matter Candidates of a Very Low Mass". *Ann. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci.* 74. [arXiv:2401.03025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.03025)

name: Composite Higgs and top condensation from BCS
summary: Technicolor and top-quark condensation replace the elementary Higgs by a fermion-pair condensate formed by a gap equation, the BCS template (one author is Bardeen of BCS); the Higgs would be composite.
sources: Bardeen, Hill & Lindner (1990). "Minimal dynamical symmetry breaking of the standard model". *Phys. Rev. D* 41, 1647. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.41.1647](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.41.1647)

name: Emergent magnetic monopoles in spin ice
summary: Defects violating the two-in-two-out ice rule behave as deconfined magnetic charges with a Coulomb interaction, a laboratory analogue of the magnetic monopoles predicted by grand unification.
breaks: Spin-ice monopoles are sources of H (div B = 0 still holds), their charge is not Dirac-quantized, and they are classical lattice defects rather than 't Hooft-Polyakov solitons of a broken gauge group.
sources: Castelnovo, Moessner & Sondhi (2008). "Magnetic monopoles in spin ice". *Nature* 451, 42. [arXiv:0710.5515](https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.5515)

name: Hedgehogs, strings and the Kibble mechanism
summary: Point and line defects in nematics are classified by the same homotopy groups as GUT monopoles and cosmic strings, and quenches through the isotropic-nematic transition test Kibble's defect-formation scenario.
breaks: Nematic defects have no gauge field, energy that scales with system size, and dissipative rather than relativistic dynamics.
sources: Chuang, Durrer, Turok & Yurke (1991). "Cosmology in the Laboratory: Defect Dynamics in Liquid Crystals". *Science* 251, 1336. [doi:10.1126/science.251.4999.1336](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.251.4999.1336)

name: Emergent supersymmetry at topological boundaries
summary: At the boundary of topological superconductors (or interacting Majorana chains) the critical point can be the tricritical Ising CFT or an N=1 Wess-Zumino theory, with exact emergent supersymmetry between bosonic order parameter and Majorana fermion.
breaks: Supersymmetry is emergent only at fine-tuned criticality and low energy; there is no superpartner spectrum or SUSY breaking scale as in the MSSM.
sources: Grover, Sheng & Vishwanath (2014). "Emergent Space-Time Supersymmetry at the Boundary of a Topological Phase". *Science* 344, 280. [arXiv:1301.7449](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.7449)

name: Type-II NbTi magnets bend the LHC beams
summary: The LHC's 8.3 T dipoles use NbTi, a type-II superconductor with strong flux pinning, cooled to 1.9 K in superfluid helium; the beam rigidity and the upper critical field set the reachable energy.

name: Silicon trackers are reverse-biased p-n junctions
summary: Pixel and strip trackers collect electron-hole pairs (3.6 eV per pair in Si) drifting in the depletion region of a reverse-biased p-n junction; radiation damage (displacement defects, type inversion) is semiconductor defect physics.
sources: Particle Data Group (2024). "Review of Particle Physics". *Phys. Rev. D* 110, 030001. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.110.030001](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.110.030001)

name: Cryogenic bolometers for 0nubb
summary: CUORE-type TeO2 crystals at ~10 mK act as calorimeters: the Debye T^3 heat capacity is tiny, so a 2.5 MeV decay raises the temperature measurably and gives keV resolution.
sources: CUORE Collaboration (2020). "Improved Limit on Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decay in 130Te with CUORE". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 124, 122501. [arXiv:1912.10966](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.10966)

name: Majorana neutrinos versus Majorana zero modes
summary: Both rest on a self-conjugate fermion psi=psi^c (gamma=gamma-dagger): an elementary Majorana neutrino would violate lepton number in 0nubb, while zero-energy Majorana modes bound to vortices or wire ends obey non-abelian exchange statistics.
breaks: Majorana zero modes are not propagating particles; they are non-abelian anyons bound to defects with no momentum or mass. Several condensed-matter Majorana claims have been retracted or reinterpreted, so evidence there is contested.
sources: Kitaev (2001). "Unpaired Majorana fermions in quantum wires". *Phys.-Usp.* 44, 131. [arXiv:cond-mat/0010440](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0010440)
Beenakker (2013). "Search for Majorana Fermions in Superconductors". *Ann. Rev. Condens. Matter Phys.* 4, 113. [arXiv:1112.1950](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.1950)
Avignone, Elliott & Engel (2008). "Double Beta Decay, Majorana Neutrinos, and Neutrino Mass". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 80, 481. [arXiv:0708.1033](https://arxiv.org/abs/0708.1033)

name: Many-body field theory: one language for both
summary: Propagators, Feynman diagrams, Matsubara sums, path integrals and the RG moved from particle QFT into many-body theory (Green's functions, Fermi liquids, Hubbard-Stratonovich), and emergent gauge theories flow back.
sources: Georges, Kotliar, Krauth & Rozenberg (1996). "Dynamical mean-field theory of strongly correlated fermion systems and the limit of infinite dimensions". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 68, 13. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.68.13](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.68.13)

name: Phase slips and macroscopic tunnelling as instantons
summary: The escape of a current-biased Josephson phase from a tilted-washboard well is a Euclidean bounce, computed with the same instanton methods as false-vacuum decay; dissipation enters through a Caldeira-Leggett bath.
sources: Coleman (1977). "Fate of the false vacuum: Semiclassical theory". *Phys. Rev. D* 15, 2929. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2929](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2929)

name: Anomaly inflow and bulk-boundary correspondence
summary: Gapless boundary modes of topological phases carry 't Hooft anomalies that are cancelled by inflow from the bulk topological response (Callan-Harvey), so the classification of topological matter is a classification of anomalies.
sources: Qi & Zhang (2011). "Topological insulators and superconductors". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 83, 1057. [arXiv:1008.2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.2026)

name: Chern-Simons theory and the parity anomaly
summary: The quantum Hall response is a Chern-Simons term whose level is the TKNN Chern number; Haldane's honeycomb model realized the 2+1D parity anomaly of a single massive Dirac fermion, the seed of Chern insulators.
sources: Haldane (1988). "Model for a Quantum Hall Effect without Landau Levels: Condensed-Matter Realization of the 'Parity Anomaly'". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 61, 2015. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.61.2015](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.61.2015)

name: Theta term and axion electrodynamics of 3D TIs
summary: The electromagnetic response of a time-reversal-invariant 3D topological insulator is a theta term with theta=pi, the same topological term as QCD's theta and the axion coupling; it implies a half-quantized surface Hall effect and the Witten effect.
map: \mathcal L_\theta=\frac{\theta e^2}{2\pi h}\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B=\frac{\theta\alpha}{4\pi^2}\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B,\ \theta=\pi;\ \sigma_{xy}^{\text{surf}}=\tfrac12\tfrac{e^2}{h}
sources: Qi & Zhang (2011). "Topological insulators and superconductors". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 83, 1057. [arXiv:1008.2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.2026)

name: Chiral (ABJ) anomaly in Weyl semimetals
summary: Parallel E and B pump electrons between Weyl nodes of opposite chirality exactly as the Adler-Bell-Jackiw anomaly; the result is a negative longitudinal magnetoresistance.
sources: Nielsen & Ninomiya (1983). "The Adler-Bell-Jackiw anomaly and Weyl fermions in a crystal". *Phys. Lett. B* 130, 389. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(83)91529-0](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(83)91529-0)

Adler (1969). "Axial-Vector Vertex in Spinor Electrodynamics". *Phys. Rev.* 177, 2426. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.177.2426](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.177.2426)

name: Graphene's massless 2+1D Dirac fermions
summary: Near the K points graphene's tight-binding bands obey the massless 2+1D Dirac equation with c replaced by v_F~c/300 and spin replaced by sublattice pseudospin, giving Klein tunnelling, a half-integer Hall sequence and optical absorption pi*alpha.
map: H=\hbar v_F\,\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf k\ \leftrightarrow\ H_D=c\,\boldsymbol\alpha\cdot\mathbf p;\ \alpha_g=\frac{e^2}{4\pi\epsilon\hbar v_F}\approx2.2,\ T=1-\pi\alpha
breaks: Lorentz invariance is only emergent at low energy; the Coulomb interaction is instantaneous (it travels at c, not v_F), so interacting graphene is not a relativistic QFT; valleys double the fermion count.
sources: Novoselov et al. (2005). "Two-dimensional gas of massless Dirac fermions in graphene". *Nature* 438, 197. [arXiv:cond-mat/0509330](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0509330)
Castro Neto et al. (2009). "The electronic properties of graphene". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 81, 109. [arXiv:0709.1163](https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.1163)
Nair et al. (2008). "Fine Structure Constant Defines Visual Transparency of Graphene". *Science* 320, 1308. [doi:10.1126/science.1156965](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1156965)

name: Weyl equation realized in TaAs
summary: Weyl semimetals host quasiparticles obeying the two-component Weyl equation that elementary physics never confirmed (neutrinos turned out massive); each node is a monopole of Berry curvature with chirality +-1.
breaks: Solid-state Weyl nodes can be tilted (type II), anisotropic and offset in energy, since there is no Lorentz symmetry, and their total number is fixed by the lattice.
sources: Xu et al. (2015). "Discovery of a Weyl fermion semimetal and topological Fermi arcs". *Science* 349, 613. [arXiv:1502.03807](https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.03807)
Armitage, Mele & Vishwanath (2018). "Weyl and Dirac semimetals in three-dimensional solids". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 90, 015001. [arXiv:1705.01111](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.01111)

name: Boundary CFT solves the multichannel Kondo problem
summary: Affleck and Ludwig treated the impurity as a conformal boundary condition of a 1+1D chiral CFT, obtaining the non-Fermi-liquid exponents and residual entropy of the overscreened multichannel Kondo fixed point.
sources: Affleck & Ludwig (1991). "Critical theory of overscreened Kondo fixed points". *Nucl. Phys. B* 360, 641. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(91)90419-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(91)90419-X)

name: Entanglement scaling reads off the central charge
summary: At a 1+1D critical point the entanglement entropy grows as (c/3) ln L, so DMRG and tensor-network simulations extract CFT central charges and operator dimensions directly from ground states.
sources: Calabrese & Cardy (2009). "Entanglement entropy and conformal field theory". *J. Phys. A* 42, 504005. [arXiv:0905.4013](https://arxiv.org/abs/0905.4013)

name: Quantum critical points as CFTs
summary: Many z=1 quantum critical points are described by conformal field theories (e.g. O(N) Wilson-Fisher in 2+1D) whose finite-T response is universal and Planckian (tau ~ hbar/k_BT); holographic CFTs model strongly coupled transport.
sources: Sachdev & Keimer (2011). "Quantum criticality". *Physics Today* 64, 29. [arXiv:1102.4628](https://arxiv.org/abs/1102.4628)

name: FQH edges and wavefunctions from CFT
summary: Edges of quantum Hall states are chiral CFTs, and bulk wavefunctions are CFT conformal blocks: the Laughlin state from a U(1) boson, the Moore-Read Pfaffian from the Ising CFT, whose sigma fields become non-abelian anyons.
sources: Moore & Read (1991). "Nonabelions in the fractional quantum Hall effect". *Nucl. Phys. B* 360, 362. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(91)90407-O](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(91)90407-O)

name: Goldstone EFT: pions and magnons
summary: Chiral perturbation theory's EFT of Goldstone bosons describes magnons: antiferromagnetic magnons are relativistic-like (O(3) sigma model, omega ~ k) while ferromagnetic ones are type-B Goldstones (omega ~ k^2) that count once per pair of broken generators.
sources: Watanabe & Murayama (2012). "Unified Description of Nambu-Goldstone Bosons without Lorentz Invariance". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 108, 251602. [arXiv:1203.0609](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.0609)
Weinberg (1979). "Phenomenological Lagrangians". *Physica A* 96, 327. [doi:10.1016/0378-4371(79)90223-1](https://doi.org/10.1016/0378-4371(79)90223-1)

name: Fermi-surface EFT: BCS as the marginal instability
summary: Treating the Fermi liquid as an EFT with RG scaling toward the Fermi surface shows only forward and BCS couplings survive, and an attractive BCS coupling is marginally relevant and runs to a gap.
sources: Shankar (1994). "Renormalization-group approach to interacting fermions". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 66, 129. [arXiv:cond-mat/9307009](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9307009)

name: Emergent QED in quantum spin ice
summary: The low-energy theory of a U(1) quantum spin liquid on the pyrochlore lattice is compact U(1) gauge theory: gapless emergent photons with omega ~ k, gapped electric charges (spinons) and magnetic monopoles.
breaks: The emergent speed of light is ~meV scale and lattice-cut off; the emergent fine-structure constant and charges are not tied to QED's, and Lorentz invariance is only approximate.
sources: Hermele, Fisher & Balents (2004). "Pyrochlore photons: The U(1) spin liquid in a S=1/2 three-dimensional frustrated magnet". *Phys. Rev. B* 69, 064404. [arXiv:cond-mat/0305401](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0305401)

name: Topological order as deconfined lattice gauge theory
summary: Z2 topological order (toric code, Z2 spin liquids) is the deconfined phase of Wegner's Z2 lattice gauge theory; anyons are its electric charges and fluxes, and the Wilson-loop perimeter law is the condensed-matter signature of deconfinement.
sources: Wegner (1971). "Duality in Generalized Ising Models and Phase Transitions without Local Order Parameters". *J. Math. Phys.* 12, 2259. [doi:10.1063/1.1665530](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1665530)
Kitaev (2003). "Fault-tolerant quantum computation by anyons". *Ann. Phys.* 303, 2. [arXiv:quant-ph/9707021](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/9707021)
Wen (1990). "Topological orders in rigid states". *Int. J. Mod. Phys. B* 4, 239. [doi:10.1142/S0217979290000139](https://doi.org/10.1142/S0217979290000139)

name: Ginzburg-Landau is the abelian Higgs model
summary: Ginzburg-Landau theory is the abelian Higgs model with charge 2e; Abrikosov vortices are Nielsen-Olesen strings and the type-I/II boundary kappa=1/sqrt2 is the BPS point where vortices do not interact.
sources: Nielsen & Olesen (1973). "Vortex-line models for dual strings". *Nucl. Phys. B* 61, 45. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(73)90350-7](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(73)90350-7)

name: Emergent gauge fields in the doped Mott insulator
summary: Slave-particle (parton) descriptions of the cuprates split the electron into spinons and holons coupled by an emergent U(1) or SU(2) gauge field, importing gauge-theory confinement and Higgs phases into high-Tc theory.
map: c_{i\sigma}=b_i^\dagger f_{i\sigma},\ \sum_\sigma f^\dagger f+b^\dagger b=1\ (\text{gauge constraint})
sources: Lee, Nagaosa & Wen (2006). "Doping a Mott insulator: Physics of high-temperature superconductivity". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 78, 17. [arXiv:cond-mat/0410445](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0410445)

name: Berry connection as a gauge field on the Brillouin zone
summary: The Berry connection is a U(1) (or, for degenerate bands, Wilczek-Zee non-abelian) gauge field over momentum space; Chern numbers are its first Chern class, the same topology as monopole and instanton charges.
sources: Berry (1984). "Quantal phase factors accompanying adiabatic changes". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 392, 45. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1984.0023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1984.0023)
Wilczek & Zee (1984). "Appearance of Gauge Structure in Simple Dynamical Systems". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 52, 2111. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.2111](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.52.2111)

name: Shared Monte Carlo, sign problem and tensor networks
summary: Lattice QCD and correlated-electron numerics share hybrid/determinant Monte Carlo and the fermion sign problem; tensor networks developed for spin chains now simulate lattice gauge theories at finite density and in real time.
map: \langle O\rangle=\frac{\int O\det M\,e^{-S}}{\int\det M\,e^{-S}},\ \det M\ \text{not positive}\Rightarrow\text{sign problem}
sources: Cataldi et al. (2024). "Simulating (2+1)D SU(2) Yang-Mills lattice gauge theory at finite density with tensor networks". [arXiv:2307.09396](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.09396)

name: Domain-wall fermions are topological boundary states
summary: Kaplan's domain-wall fermions get lattice chiral fermions as zero modes bound to a mass domain wall in one higher dimension, the same Jackiw-Rebbi mechanism that produces protected surface Dirac cones of topological insulators.
map: (i\gamma^\mu\partial_\mu-m(s))\psi=0,\ m(s)\to\pm m\ \Rightarrow\ \psi_0\propto e^{-\int^s m(s')ds'}\ (\text{chiral zero mode})
sources: Kaplan (1992). "A Method for simulating chiral fermions on the lattice". *Phys. Lett. B* 288, 342. [arXiv:hep-lat/9206013](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-lat/9206013)

name: Nielsen-Ninomiya doubling forces paired Weyl nodes
summary: The no-go theorem that lattice chiral fermions come in pairs of opposite chirality is the reason Weyl nodes in a crystal always appear in pairs, and Nielsen and Ninomiya themselves proposed the crystal chiral anomaly.
sources: Nielsen & Ninomiya (1983). "The Adler-Bell-Jackiw anomaly and Weyl fermions in a crystal". *Phys. Lett. B* 130, 389. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(83)91529-0](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(83)91529-0)

name: Running Fermi velocity in graphene
summary: Coulomb interactions renormalize graphene's Fermi velocity logarithmically, like a running coupling, because alpha_g is marginal; suspended graphene shows the predicted log enhancement near the Dirac point.
sources: Elias et al. (2011). "Dirac cones reshaped by interaction effects in suspended graphene". *Nature Phys.* 7, 701. [arXiv:1104.1396](https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.1396)

name: Kondo temperature as dimensional transmutation
summary: The antiferromagnetic Kondo coupling is marginally relevant, so it grows at low energy like an asymptotically free coupling and generates a scale T_K exactly as Lambda_QCD emerges; Wilson's numerical RG solved it.
breaks: Kondo is a 0+1D impurity problem with no gauge field or confinement; the strong-coupling fixed point is a screened singlet (Fermi liquid), not a confined hadron spectrum.
sources: Wilson (1975). "The Renormalization Group: Critical Phenomena and the Kondo Problem". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 47, 773. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.47.773](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.47.773)

name: DMRG born from the failure of real-space RG
summary: White's DMRG replaced Wilson-style energy truncation by density-matrix truncation, turning real-space renormalization into the most accurate 1D many-body method and the seed of tensor-network RG.
sources: White (1992). "Density matrix formulation for quantum renormalization groups". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 69, 2863. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.69.2863](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.69.2863)

name: Could photons and electrons be emergent?
summary: String-net condensation produces emergent U(1) gauge bosons and fermionic charges from local bosonic spins, suggesting the Standard Model's gauge fields and fermions might themselves be emergent.
breaks: No string-net model reproduces chiral fermions, non-abelian SU(3)xSU(2)xU(1), or exact Lorentz invariance; chiral gauge theories resist lattice regularization.
sources: Levin & Wen (2005). "Colloquium: Photons and electrons as emergent phenomena". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 77, 871. [arXiv:cond-mat/0407140](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0407140)

name: Higgs mechanism first appeared as the Meissner effect
summary: The idea that a condensate gives a gauge field mass migrated from superconductivity (London, Nambu, Anderson) to the Standard Model's electroweak sector.
sources: Nambu (1960). "Quasi-Particles and Gauge Invariance in the Theory of Superconductivity". *Phys. Rev.* 117, 648. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.117.648](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.117.648)

name: Anderson-Higgs mechanism: photon mass = W mass
summary: A superconductor's Cooper-pair condensate eats the phase Goldstone mode and gives the photon a mass 1/lambda_L (Meissner effect), the same abelian Higgs mechanism that gives W and Z masses from the Higgs vev.
map: m_\gamma c^2=\frac{\hbar c}{\lambda_L},\ \lambda_L^{-2}=\mu_0n_se^2/m\ \leftrightarrow\ m_W=\tfrac12gv;\ \Delta\leftrightarrow\langle H\rangle,\ 2e\leftrightarrow g
breaks: The SC condensate is a composite of electrons, non-relativistic and in a medium with a preferred frame; the electroweak condensate is (as far as known) elementary and Lorentz invariant, and its gauge group is non-abelian.
sources: Anderson (1963). "Plasmons, Gauge Invariance, and Mass". *Phys. Rev.* 130, 439. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.130.439](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.130.439)
Higgs (1964). "Broken Symmetries and the Masses of Gauge Bosons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 508. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.508](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.508)

name: Higgs amplitude mode in superconductors
summary: The Higgs boson is the amplitude oscillation of the condensate; superconductors have the same mode at energy 2Delta, observed in Raman and terahertz pump-probe experiments.
breaks: In a superconductor the mode sits at the pair-breaking edge and can decay into quasiparticles; its observation needs coupling via a CDW or nonlinear drive since it is Raman- but not dipole-active.
sources: Pekker & Varma (2015). "Amplitude/Higgs Modes in Condensed Matter Physics". *Ann. Rev. Condens. Matter Phys.* 6, 269. [arXiv:1406.2968](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.2968)
Matsunaga et al. (2014). "Light-induced collective pseudospin precession resonating with Higgs mode in a superconductor". *Science* 345, 1145. [arXiv:1407.4554](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.4554)

name: Color superconductivity in dense quark matter
summary: At high baryon density attractive one-gluon exchange in the color antitriplet channel makes quarks Cooper-pair near the Fermi surface; in the CFL phase the diquark condensate Higgses all eight gluons (color Meissner effect).
sources: Alford, Rajagopal & Wilczek (1999). "Color-flavor locking and chiral symmetry breaking in high density QCD". *Nucl. Phys. B* 537, 443. [arXiv:hep-ph/9804403](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9804403)

name: Confinement as a dual Meissner effect
summary: If chromomagnetic monopoles condense, chromoelectric flux is squeezed into tubes just as magnetic flux is in a type-II superconductor, giving a linear quark potential with string tension sigma.
breaks: The roles of E and B are swapped, the gauge group is non-abelian, and monopole condensation in QCD is gauge-dependent and unproven analytically.
sources: 't Hooft (1981). "Topology of the gauge condition and new confinement phases in non-Abelian gauge theories". *Nucl. Phys. B* 190, 455. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(81)90442-9](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(81)90442-9)
Nielsen & Olesen (1973). "Vortex-line models for dual strings". *Nucl. Phys. B* 61, 45. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(73)90350-7](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(73)90350-7)

name: NJL: chiral symmetry breaking modelled on BCS
summary: Nambu and Jona-Lasinio built dynamical mass generation for nucleons by direct analogy with the BCS gap equation; the massless Goldstone mode of the analogy became the pion, a precursor of QCD chiral symmetry breaking.
sources: Nambu & Jona-Lasinio (1961). "Dynamical Model of Elementary Particles Based on an Analogy with Superconductivity. I". *Phys. Rev.* 122, 345. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.122.345](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.122.345)
Bardeen, Cooper & Schrieffer (1957). "Theory of Superconductivity". *Phys. Rev.* 108, 1175. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.108.1175](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.108.1175)

name: Radiation damage in reactor materials
summary: Fast neutrons create displacement cascades in fuel cladding, steels and graphite; point-defect production, swelling, embrittlement and stored Wigner energy are solid-state physics that limits reactor lifetimes and fusion first walls.
breaks: Displacement counts overestimate surviving defects because of in-cascade recombination, so molecular dynamics is needed.
sources: Kinchin & Pease (1955). "The Displacement of Atoms in Solids by Radiation". *Rep. Prog. Phys.* 18, 1. [doi:10.1088/0034-4885/18/1/301](https://doi.org/10.1088/0034-4885/18/1/301)

name: Neutron transmutation doping of silicon
summary: Irradiating float-zone silicon in a reactor turns 30Si into 31P by neutron capture and beta decay, giving the most uniform n-type doping available, used for high-power devices and thyristors.
breaks: Only n-type doping is possible, and the lattice damage has to be annealed.

name: Semiconductor and scintillator radiation detectors
summary: HPGe and Si detectors are reverse-biased p-n junctions whose energy resolution is set by electron-hole pair statistics (about 3 eV per pair, Fano factor ~0.1); scintillators and halide-perovskite detectors depend on excitons, traps and band gaps.
breaks: Detector-grade operation needs ultrapure crystals with long carrier lifetimes and radiation hardness, priorities different from electronic devices.
sources: Fano (1947). "Ionization Yield of Radiations. II. The Fluctuations of the Number of Ions". *Phys. Rev.* 72, 26. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.72.26](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.72.26)

summary: Near charge neutrality graphene electrons form a Dirac fluid described by the same relativistic viscous hydrodynamics as the QGP, with c replaced by v_F; it was predicted and then measured to be a nearly perfect fluid with low eta/s that violates Wiedemann-Franz.

name: Colour superconductivity in dense quark matter
summary: At high baryon density the attractive colour-antitriplet channel makes the quark Fermi surface unstable to BCS pairing; the colour-flavour-locked phase is a colour superconductor in which gluons acquire Meissner masses and chiral symmetry breaks, a candidate for neutron-star cores.
breaks: The condensate breaks a non-abelian gauge symmetry and is under control only at asymptotic density; at neutron-star densities it is model-dependent and has no direct experimental confirmation.

name: Viscous electron flow and eta/s in metals vs QGP
summary: In ultraclean conductors electron-electron collisions dominate and charge flows hydrodynamically (Gurzhi effect, negative nonlocal resistance), giving measured electron viscosities that can be set against QGP eta/s in the same Navier-Stokes framework.
breaks: Fermi-liquid electrons are weakly coupled with a long l_ee, so their eta/s is far above the QGP value; momentum relaxation at boundaries and impurities has no QGP counterpart.

name: Spin-vorticity: Lambda polarization and Barnett effect
summary: Global Lambda polarization in off-central collisions shows the QGP is the most vortical fluid known; it aligns spins through the same spin-rotation coupling as the Barnett effect and spin hydrodynamic generation in liquid metals.
breaks: QGP polarization is read from the hadronized final state of a ~10 fm/c fluid in local equilibrium; the spintronic versions involve electron spin, spin-orbit coupling and dissipative spin currents.

name: Planckian dissipation: QGP and strange metals
summary: The QGP's eta/s near hbar/(4 pi k_B) and the strange-metal scattering rate hbar/tau of order k_BT are both 'Planckian' transport set by hbar and T alone, and gauge/gravity duality has been applied to both as a model of strongly coupled matter without quasiparticles.
breaks: Strange-metal resistivity needs momentum relaxation by the lattice and disorder, while eta/s is a momentum-conserving diffusivity; the KSS value is not a proven bound, and holographic models are neither QCD nor cuprates.
sources: Kovtun, Son & Starinets (2005). "Viscosity in Strongly Interacting Quantum Field Theories from Black Hole Physics". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 94, 111601. [arXiv:hep-th/0405231](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0405231)

Hartnoll (2015). "Theory of universal incoherent metallic transport". *Nature Phys.* 11, 54. [arXiv:1405.3651](https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.3651)

name: Chiral condensate modelled on the BCS gap (NJL)
summary: Nambu and Jona-Lasinio built dynamical chiral symmetry breaking by direct analogy with BCS: the quark mass gap is a fermion-pair condensate, and its melting at the QCD crossover is the chiral-restoration signature studied in heavy-ion collisions.
breaks: The chiral condensate pairs particles with antiparticles and breaks a global, not a gauge, symmetry, so it gives Goldstone pions instead of a Meissner effect; the QCD transition is a crossover.

name: Chiral anomaly: CME in QGP and Weyl semimetals
summary: The axial anomaly that would drive a current along B in a chirally imbalanced QGP (the chiral magnetic effect) is the same anomaly equation behind the negative longitudinal magnetoresistance of Weyl and Dirac semimetals, where the effect is observed; in heavy-ion collisions the isobar run found no signal beyond background.
breaks: In the QGP the imbalance comes from gluon topological fluctuations and B lasts ~0.1 fm/c; in Weyl metals it is pumped by parallel E and B and relaxed by internode scattering, and lattice Weyl nodes come in pairs (Nielsen-Ninomiya).
sources: Fukushima, Kharzeev & Warringa (2008). "The Chiral Magnetic Effect". *Phys. Rev. D* 78, 074033. [arXiv:0808.3382](https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.3382)
Li et al. (2016). "Chiral magnetic effect in ZrTe5". *Nature Phys.* 12, 550. [arXiv:1412.6543](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.6543)

name: Band theory of dripped neutrons in the inner crust
summary: Free neutrons in the inner crust move in the periodic potential of the nuclear lattice, so Bloch band structure gives them an effective mass and entrainment by the crust; band calculations find most neutrons entrained, which feeds the glitch angular-momentum budget.
map: \psi_{n\mathbf k}(\mathbf r+\mathbf R)=e^{i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf R}\psi_{n\mathbf k}(\mathbf r);\ n_n^{c}\propto\sum_{n\mathbf k}|\nabla_{\mathbf k}\epsilon_{n\mathbf k}|^2\delta(\epsilon-\mu)
breaks: Pairing, with a gap comparable to band splittings, smears band effects and is often neglected in band calculations; that is the main open question.
sources: Chamel (2012). "Neutron conduction in the inner crust of a neutron star in the framework of the band theory of solids". *Phys. Rev. C* 85, 035801. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevC.85.035801](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevC.85.035801)

name: Neutron-star crust as a bcc Coulomb crystal
summary: The outer crust is a body-centred-cubic lattice of neutron-rich nuclei in a degenerate relativistic electron gas; its composition follows from minimizing Madelung plus nuclear energies, and inner-crust calculations use the Wigner-Seitz cell method taken from solid-state physics.
breaks: The lattice 'atoms' are bare nuclei in a uniform relativistic electron gas (no chemical bonding), and the inner crust is penetrated by a neutron superfluid.
sources: Chamel & Haensel (2008). "Physics of Neutron Star Crusts". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 11, 10. [arXiv:0812.3955](https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.3955)

name: Crust transport: conductivity, impurities and field decay
summary: Crust thermal and electrical conductivities are computed with metal transport theory (electron-phonon and electron-impurity scattering, Wiedemann-Franz); crust cooling after accretion outbursts shows a well-ordered, high-conductivity lattice, while a disordered pasta layer would be highly resistive.
breaks: The electrons are ultra-relativistic and fields reach 1e15 G, so magnetized quantum transport goes beyond terrestrial regimes.
sources: Brown & Cumming (2009). "Mapping Crustal Heating with the Cooling Light Curves of Quasi-Persistent Transients". *Astrophys. J.* 698, 1020. [arXiv:0901.3115](https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.3115)

name: Crust elasticity, phonons and magnetar oscillations
summary: The crust shear modulus and breaking strain come from the lattice dynamics of the Coulomb crystal (molecular dynamics gives a strain of ~0.1, far above terrestrial metals); crust torsional modes are candidates for magnetar-flare QPOs, and crust strength limits the mountains that would radiate gravitational waves.
breaks: Phonons of a Coulomb crystal in a compressible electron background have a plasma-frequency longitudinal branch, unlike the acoustic phonons of ordinary solids; superfluid neutrons add mixed modes.

name: Nuclear pasta as liquid-crystal-like matter
summary: Rod and slab pasta phases have orientational and partial positional order like columnar and smectic liquid crystals, so their elasticity and topological defects (screw dislocations in slabs) are described with liquid-crystal elastic theory; this sets the pasta shear modulus and viscosity.
breaks: Pasta units are nuclear clusters ordered by Coulomb frustration, not anisotropic molecules; there is no molecular director and thermal fluctuations are weak.
sources: Caplan & Horowitz (2017). "Colloquium: Astromaterial science and nuclear pasta". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 89, 041002. [arXiv:1606.03646](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.03646)

name: Nuclear pasta and block-copolymer microphase separation
summary: Pasta phases (spheres, rods, slabs, gyroid-like and inverted) come from competition between nuclear surface tension and long-range Coulomb energy; block-copolymer melts show the same morphology sequence because the Ohta-Kawasaki functional has the same short-range plus Coulomb-kernel structure.
breaks: Pasta is cold, quantum-degenerate matter with shell effects and electron screening; copolymer morphology is set by chain entropy and connectivity at finite temperature, and kinetics and defects differ.
